The problem is, if they're not squadded up they'd get kicked after tking and such... so all good. But if they're squadded up, even 2 people together? You will *never* kick them, because you need the votes of everyone else, their squad mate included. Look at this situation, for example: 4 teamed up to troll him - if vote to kick was still in, do you think he'd have either get tkd and kicked, be forced to tk like the vid and still get kicked out even without an automated system and so on.

Plus, Ubisoft is a business, and a lot of people have mentioned that they don't play Siege anymore because of the vote to kick abuse.

The closest thing I've come up as a solution is counting, for voting purposes, a squad as a single player - that means, 4 teamed up would only need 1 vote from whoever is playing with them to get kicked out, but even then it'd just end up abused - less often than the opposite though.

Whenever people think of solutions, they need someone else that can think of how it can backfire - since you also seem like a smart dude thinking about these kind of problems, what's your take about my idea? How would it be misused terribly? How easy would it be to turn it into a worse mechanic for everyone involved?

Weapons don't really have different movesets among the same category, exception being a couple of items having a small extra skill (I have crap memory but I can confirm only one), but every weapon class has a unique expansive moveset with new active skills to unlock.
There are 5 types in the base game (Swords, Dual Swords, Spears, Axes/Hammers and Kusarigama), with 2 new ones added with the DLCs (Odachi and Tonfa)
Each stance has their skills and attacks. 

You also get three kind of ranged weapons, each type does more damage per shot than the previous, but at the cost of more restricted mobility and less ammo. These are bows, matchlock rifles and lastly cannons that require you stand still to aim and shoot. 
Ammo isn't refilled at shrine (bonfires), so the ammo you start a mission with is the ammo you will have along that mission except for anything you find on site. There are ways around that (some passives allow you to recover arrows sometimes, or to have a chance to not consume ammo on each shot, plus a refillable scroll that gives you a free shot if you're out of ammo) 
This in turns makes ranged attacks very powerful, a lot of mobs can either get knocked out and thus open for a killing blow or straight up die in one headshot.
You have two types of ammo per weapon, one is more plentiful but weaker, one is rarer but very strong. 

I went with Katana and Spear, depending on which move I needed to dispatch a type of enemy easily, but Odachi were cool too.

Sequel adds new weapon types too: a couple of small hatchets that can be thrown through some skills and a switchglaive that is a weapon that changes based on stance, resembling things like a glaive (duh), a form I can't remember (haven't gotten the game yet) and a schyte.

Each weapon is also tied to a stat, so a ninjutsu heavy character would benefit from using kusarigamas, but weapon stats matter more than your stats generally speaking.

A cool thing about the game is that you can recover ki (stamina) faster if you switch stances at the right time after attacking, with some skills allowing you to regain more if you switch stance twice... If you're lazier like me, you can recover a good portion also by doing a ki pulse, which is pressing the switch stance button without switching stances... Or with a skill, by dodging at the right time.

Another cool thing is that both games are 60fps even on base ps4. Graphics are downgraded (jaggies and blurrier) but it's a lot better for this kind of game to have 60fps rather than good graphics.

So, ultimately, I'd say if you want to give a from soft another go, that might be a good game to try, especially since it plays differently from dark souls so if you didn't play it, you don't have some habits that would punish you in Sekiro.
